label: rem:beta-stability-interpretation
title: Derivation, verification, and limiting behaviour of beta-stability
html:
Derivation. At fixed A, beta decay converts \mathfrak{n} \to \mathfrak{p} (or vice versa) while preserving A. We minimize the mass M(p, A) = p \cdot m_{\mathfrak{p}} + (A-p) \cdot m_{\mathfrak{n}} - \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{bind}}(p, A-p) by setting \partial M / \partial p \big|_A = 0:

  (m_{\mathfrak{p}} - m_{\mathfrak{n}})
  + \frac{a_C  (2p - 1)}{A^{1/3}}
  - \frac{a_A  (A - 2p)}{A}
  = 0.

Solving for p:

  a_A  \frac{A - 2p}{A}
  = a_C  \frac{2p}{A^{1/3}},
  \qquad
  p = \frac{A}{2 + a_C  A^{2/3} / (2a_A)}.

Verification. At q = q_0, with a_C = (q - q^{-1}) \times 3.334 \approx 0.697 MeV and a_A \approx 23.29 MeV, the formula reproduces the observed stable neutron numbers across the periodic table. The mean error is |\Delta n| \approx 1.4 neutrons.

Limiting behaviour.

Regime q a_C n^*/p Physics
Classical q \to 1 0 1.00 No Coulomb; all nuclei symmetric
Our universe q = q_0 0.70 1.0--1.6 Valley of stability
Deep quantum q \to \infty \to \infty \to \infty Coulomb overwhelms; no heavy nuclei

The entire nuclear chart follows from the single parameter q.
